Firstly, I'm really enjoying the show and look forward to it every week. Most of what I've seen around here is nothing but praise for it, and while I think a lot of that is deserved, I wanted to offer some things that have been bugging me in order to balance it out.

I really enjoy the tech in the show. I like the references to various things that non-tech people might not get. Lately, however, I've been feeling they've been stretching it a bit as far as technical ability. I don't know, it just feels like Elliot and the dream team in the basement are able to do everything and anything in an unbelievably short amount of time. I know, I know, it's just a show and they need to be able to keep the story moving along at an exciting pace, but it's like they've got the tech resources/prowess of a 1st world government behind them despite only being a few people. Hell, I won't even be surprised if they claim they reverse engineered stuxnet or took over PRISM or something.

Which leads me to another thing: State actors seem to be completely missing from the show. Yeah, Evil Corp is the main nebulous "bad guy" in the series, but it seems like the whole NSA angle is missing. The only time the government is present in the series is your average street cop.

Furthermore, how can Elliot keep his job? He works in a cubicle farm and yet seems to have the autonomy of being able to come and go when he pleases. I don't think we've actually seen him do any real work in the series besides fly on a jet to save evil corp during the very first episode. Also, Out of band management anyone? They shouldn't have to fly on a jet to physically connect to some server farm, but that's a lot less dramatic. Though so too would be Elliot working and reading through security logs all day...

Perhaps the biggest criticism I have of the show is that I don't really care about the non-tech centric story lines. Tyrell trying to become CTO? He's scary and psychotic as fuck, yes, but I watch the show for cyberpunk elements, not a drama about scheming executives trying to get to the top. Same goes for the Angela/Colby/environmental disaster stuff. I can't help but feel that these extra sub plots were put in the show to try and make it appeal to a wider audience that's not super techy, which is understandable, the show has to make money, but I feel it's a bit drift from the main focus and strength of the show.

Just my 2 cents. Still love it overall.
